memory_verse.label: Bible Portion
memory_verse.text: "As they sat down to eat their meal, they looked up and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were loaded with spices, balm and myrrh, and they were on their way to take them down to Egypt" - Gen 37:25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
One small detail in this verse is deeply disturbing: having thrown their brother into a pit, the brothers "sat down to eat their meal." Just steps away, Joseph was crying out from the darkness — and they calmly ate. Years later they would remember this very moment with shame, recalling "how distressed he was when he pleaded with us for his life, but we would not listen" (Gen 42:21). They hardened their hearts and enjoyed their food while their brother suffered.

This is what sin does to the conscience. It numbs us, so that we can do terrible things and feel nothing at the time. The brothers could eat comfortably because they had silenced the voice inside them. It is frightening how calloused the human heart can become when it refuses to listen to conscience.

Let this sober us. Are there cries we have learned to eat comfortably beside — needs we ignore, people we have wronged, a conscience we have quietly muffled? God calls us to keep our hearts tender, quick to hear both His voice and the cries of those around us (Heb 3:15).

Notice too the caravan appearing on the horizon. Even in this callous moment, God was at work behind the scenes, guiding events. The very traders who would carry Joseph to Egypt were arriving at exactly the right time. God's providence was moving, unseen, through it all.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Are there cries you have learned to ignore comfortably?
Is your conscience tender, or have you let it grow numb?
Can you trust that God is at work even in dark moments?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep my heart tender and my conscience alive. Do not let me grow numb to the cries around me. And help me to trust that You are at work even when I cannot see it. Amen.
